summary: Learn forensic accounting and fraud investigation with evidence tracing, interviews, and reporting. Build practical tools in 5 days.
lede: Forensic accounting combines accounting, audit and investigative methods to detect irregularities and reconstruct transactions. Designed for professionals working with financial records, controls, investigations or compliance reviews, the course covers fraud risk assessment, transaction-data analysis and investigation planning, including evidence logs and interview questions. Learners also practice tracing account movements and presenting documented findings in concise fraud reports.
audienceIntro: This advanced course is designed for professionals who already work with financial records, control testing, investigations, or compliance review and need deeper forensic capability.
outcomes: Evidence Preservation And Chain Of Custody
prerequisites: Advanced-level familiarity with accounting entries, financial statements, audit procedures, and internal controls is expected. You should be comfortable working with spreadsheets, reviewing source documents, and interpreting transaction flows. Prior exposure to fraud examination, investigative interviewing, or compliance review is helpful but not mandatory. No programming is required, although familiarity with data filtering, pivot tables, and basic analytics workflows will help you get more from the hands-on exercises.
